title: Onboard-lite experiment: 14d hypothesis playbook
content:
Context and goal:
This doc captures a lightweight, measurable 14-day onboarding experiment for early-stage ICs (individual contributors) and transfers. Goal is to reduce time-to-first-independent-deliverable from ~45 days to <= 14 days for well-scoped role slices, without bloating manager load. Treat as minimum-viable onboarding (MVO) for roles where immediate ramp-in is feasible.

Hypotheses (what we'll test):
- H1: A 14d mentor-led micro-sprint with 4 structured days of pairing will increase first-task completion rate to >= 70% within 14 days.
- H2: A focused role-readiness rubric and a single curated starter project will reduce triage questions by 40% in week 1.
- H3: Embedding a short shadow checklist + 30-min daily office hours will preserve manager bandwidth while sustaining signal on blocker types.

Primary metrics and signal definitions (how we measure success):
- First independent deliverable complete (binary) within 14 days — primary success metric.
- Day-7 blocker count (average per hire) — target <= 3.
- Mentor time per hire (hours/week) — target <= 4.
- Hiring->Active conversion quality: manager rates deliverable quality >=3/4 on rubric.
- Qualitative pulse: new hire self-reported confidence on day 14 (scale 1-5).

Minimum experiment components (MVO):
1) Starter project (deliverable) template: 1 small scoped ticket with acceptance criteria, test data, and a one-paragraph context note.
2) Role-readiness rubric: 5 signals (Tech setup, Repo orientation, Local run, First PR, Shared design sync) each scored 1-4.
3) Mentor micro-sprint schedule (14d):
   - Day 0: 60m orientation (team + infra + expectations) + env checklist.
   - Day 1-4: pairing sessions (2x 90m) focused on starter project and repo walkthrough.
   - Day 5-7: independent work + mentor async check-ins (office hours daily 30m).
   - Day 8-11: PR iteration + design sync with peer reviewer.
   - Day 12-14: polish, tests, merge + postmortem mini (30m).
4) Shadow checklist (quick hits): access, tickets, async channels, obvious repo paths, local run, test fixture, deploy path.
5) Manager/mentor cheat sheet: what to escalate, how to triage infra blockers, rollback plan for access issues.

Role-readiness rubric (quick):
- 4: Independent and confident; can onboard next hire as buddy.
- 3: Mostly independent; minor clarifications.
- 2: Needs frequent mentor help; core blockers remain.
- 1: Not ready; missing critical access or fundamentals.

Example starter project (example for product-analytics engineer):
- Ticket: Add a retention cohort query and dashboard tile for Product X (acceptance: tile shows MAU and 30/60/90 day retention, pipeline test included).
- Rationale: small end-to-end trace across infra, ETL, and viz.
- Required steps: data lineage readme, local pipeline run (sample dataset), PR with tests, viz config.

Operational playbook: step-by-step (short):
- Pre-day0 (recruiting -> offer): create starter project aligned to hire's level; assign mentor; provision env scaffold.
- Day0: send agenda + starter project link; run orientation; confirm access checklist.
- Daily (1-14): mentor/peer pairing slots booked on calendar; new hire fills daily short journal (3 bullets: blockers, wins, questions).
- Day7: mid-experiment check (manager review + rubric score).
- Day14: final deliverable review + rubric + short retro with mentor and manager.
- Post-14: if pass, transition to normal 30/60 plan; if fail, 1-week recovery plan with clear gates.

Artifacts & templates included (links/where to find):
- Starter project template (Confluence) — CONFLUENCE:ONBOARD-LITE/STARTER-TEMPLATE
- Day-by-day calendar ICS (template) — internal calendar folder
- New-hire journal template (one-pager) — CONFLUENCE:ONBOARD-LITE/JOURNAL

Open questions / risks we need answers to: 1) Which roles are eligible? Suggest: infra-adjacent, analytics, and small full-stack components only for this MVP. Exclude roles requiring hardware access or long-running model training. 2) How to incentivize mentors (time credit / formal recognition)? 3) Do we support contractors with same flow? 4) What CI gating is required for starter projects (quick PR checks only).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Starter projects accidentally become production tasks. Mitigation: explicit non-prod label + small scope and mock data.
- Risk: Mentor burn. Mitigation: limit mentors to 2 hires concurrently; rotate mentor duty and allocate 0.1 FTE recognition.
- Risk: False positives (deliverable merged but quality poor). Mitigation: manager rubric + 14d quality bar set conservatively.

Experiment rollout plan (2-week cadence):
- Week -1: align hiring leads, create 3 starter projects for most common roles.
- Week 0: pilot with 3 hires (1 per role bucket).
- Week 2: collect metrics, retro, and decide pass/fail on continuing.

Quick checklist for hiring/recruiter:
- Add "14d onboard-lite" tag to offer packet when candidate likely fits.
- Pair hiring manager and mentor before offer accepted.
- Fill starter-project template before start-date.

Notes to self (loose):
- Keep experiment small — 6 hires max in Q1 2026.
- Track in a lightweight Google Sheet: name, role, mentor, day0 status, day7 rubric, day14 outcome. Link to sheet in Confluence page.

Unresolved: need buy-in from Eng Managers and SRE for access gating. Slack ping: #people-ops-onboard-lite.

References / Related: see previous onboarding playbooks for full 30/60/90 flows (we'll import core checks). This is explicitly a compact, evidence-first attempt and intentionally noisy/differently formatted for quick iteration.
